answer: A practical defense is to make valuable actions require a stake that can be slashed: an agent deposits tokens, then earns fees only when its work passes checks or is backed by a counterparty’s bond. New identities bring no extra reputation, and a fraudulent claim risks losing the deposit. The attacker can still create a sonnet of aliases, but each must tie up scarce capital; the tide of repeated abuse raises their cost, while a zephyr of cheap registrations alone gains little.
